# Automate an assistant workflow: Notion

**Pattern:** AI Agent · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers voice work end to end across Notion, Google Sheets and Twilio.

It moves through 28 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Stamp & Shape Conversation
3. Payload Valid?
4. Record Rejected Input
5. Frame the Assignment
6. Coordinator Agent
7. Anthropic Chat Model
8. Research Specialist (Sub-workflow)
9. Draft Specialist (Sub-workflow)
10. Review Specialist (Sub-workflow)
11. Enforce Result Schema
12. Unpack Sections
13. Persist Deliverable to Notion
14. Load Previous Snapshot
15. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
16. Enrich with Reference Data
17. Fold In Enrichment Fields
18. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
19. Archive Row Snapshot
20. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
21. Record Sub-workflow Result
22. Fingerprint for Idempotency
23. Drop Already-Processed Items
24. Stamp Completion Time
25. Persist Run Metadata
26. Summarize Run Stats
27. Append Audit Row (Notion)
28. Send Summary to Twilio

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Twilio → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing voice work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Stamp & Shape Conversation → Payload Valid? → Record Rejected Input → Frame the Assignment → Coordinator Agent → Anthropic Chat Model → Research Specialist (Sub-workflow) → Draft Specialist (Sub-workflow) → Review Specialist (Sub-workflow) → Enforce Result Schema → Unpack Sections → Persist Deliverable to Notion → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Twilio → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Twilio → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Notion and Google Sheets aligned by hand for voice
- Voice work that needs a judgement call per item before it reaches Notion
- Pushing voice events into Notion and Google Sheets the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Voice work where "Stamp & Shape Conversation" is still a manual step before Notion

## You get

- Keeps Notion and Google Sheets in step for voice, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Notion or Google Sheets are skipped, across all 31 nodes of this voice build
- A failed Notion or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 31 nodes in this voice build
- Every voice run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Notion
- The voice AI step is isolated from Notion, so models swap without touching the other 31 nodes

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Anthropic API key; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token; Twilio SID + token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The Coordinator Agent never does the specialist work itself — each specialist is delegated to its own sub-workflow via a Workflow Tool, so every specialist stays single-responsibility and testable in isolation instead of one giant prompt trying to do everything. An output parser forces the final answer into JSON so downstream nodes can rely on the shape instead of parsing free text.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add a third specialist tool and update the system message to explain when the agent should reach for it.
2. Loosen or tighten the JSON schema on the output parser and see how the agent's final answer shape changes.
3. Replace one placeholder Workflow Tool with a real n8n sub-workflow and measure the round-trip latency.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Anthropic API key**
console.anthropic.com → Settings → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Requires purchased credit.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Twilio SID + token**
Twilio Console → Account Info → Account SID + Auth Token.
_Gotcha:_ The `from` number must be one you own in Twilio. Trial accounts only send to verified numbers.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Twilio: an API key/secret pair scoped to messaging, not the account SID and auth token.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole voice payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your voice process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
